481	a gentile who comes to convert is always warned first.
482	Think carefully about whether you want to do
483	this. Judaism is not like other religions, where the main thing is
484	just come, just join
485	us, become Muslim, become Christian, become Buddhist.
486	Judaism is not like that. A gentile who comes to convert is told:
487	"Think carefully about whether you want to do this.
488	Because as long as you are a gentile and you drive on Shabbat, you
489	are not punished for it, because you are a gentile. There is no prohibition.
490	The gentiles are obligated in seven mitzvot. There is no mitzvah
491	of keeping Shabbat. The seven mitzvot — what are the seven mitzvot
492	that gentiles are obligated in? They are easy to remember. Three of the
493	seven are the three gravest transgressions in the Torah,
494	for which the law is: be killed rather than transgress. The prohibition of idolatry,
495	forbidden relations, bloodshed. How many are left? Four
496	mitzvot. Eiver min hachai: a gentile is forbidden to torment
497	animals, but he is not required to slaughter. He may
498	kill an animal and eat. With us, only
499	proper slaughter is allowed. And he may eat any
500	animal he wants. With us, only what the Torah
501	permitted: chewing the cud, split hooves, fins
502	and scales
503	in fish. But he is forbidden to torment
504	animals. So that is eiver min hachai. Second, blessing
505	HaShem's Name. This is in euphemistic language, reversed language. Instead of
506	saying cursing HaShem, we say blessing, because it is not
507	nice to speak of curses. That is, even when disaster
508	strikes a gentile, he is forbidden to rail against Elokim, to come
509	in anger. Rely on the Creator of the world, who knows what
510	He did, believe
511	in Him. The next mitzvah is robbery: he is forbidden
512	to steal. And the last one, the seventh, is laws.
513	They must establish a legal system of
514	civil law. They can invent their own laws. Not like
515	with us, where even civil law must be according to
516	the Torah. They can invent laws, but the main thing is
517	that there be order among people, that they have laws
518	for neighbors, quarrels, disputes, that everything
519	be such that they do not take advantage of one another. We are all human beings and must keep
520	fairness. To remember the seven mitzvot, it is very
521	easy. Three are the three
522	gravest transgressions: idolatry, forbidden relations, bloodshed.
523	The other four, a mnemonic came out like this: the initials
524	of them are alef, bet, gimel, dalet: eiver min hachai, blessing HaShem,
525	robbery, laws of civil matters. These are the seven mitzvot of
526	the gentiles. A gentile who says "I want more," on the contrary,
527	let him convert and then he connects to everything. They just tell him
528	in advance: think whether you want to obligate yourself, think carefully,
529	because afterwards if you desecrate Shabbat there will be a claim against you, you will
530	be punished. A Jew is born into this and is obligated; you are not
531	obligated.
532	
533	If you want to increase your connection to the Creator
534	of the world, then please,
535	it is your right. But the people of Israel has an ideal that it be good
536	for all of humanity, and therefore in the Beit HaMikdash there was a
537	special service to bring down great
538	abundance. Let us now move on to the mechanism that Shlomo HaMelech built
539	in the Beit HaMikdash. When he built the Beit HaMikdash on top of Mount Moriah,
540	he invested enormous resources there. The walls were covered with
541	gold. Whoever looks at the verses: you enter a
542	great hall, all the walls covered in gold. Besides the Menorah
543	of the Mishkan and the Table of the showbread that Moshe Rabbeinu made,
544	which were made entirely of pure gold, he made 12 more
545	golden menorahs. And the same with the tables of the showbread.
546	Like the showbread table, he made 12 more.
547	That is, the wealth in the Beit HaMikdash was legendary
548	wealth, and all of it splendor and glory for the honor of HaShem. And one can
549	see in the verses in the Book of Melachim everything Shlomo did,
550	how he built the Beit HaMikdash. There was a hall there
551	of
552	pillars whose tops were magnificent capitals. Which, by the way,
553	we brought also in the book on archaeology, also here
554	in volume 3 there are such
555	capitals. What was found in the archaeological digs was put
556	on the 5 shekel coin. There is such a capital
557	today; you can see there that it is the capital of a pillar.
558	They were always sure that this capital, which is like
559	two cylinders around and joined
560	at the top, was given a Greek name, because they were sure
561	it was a Greek idea. In the archaeological digs
562	they suddenly found such capitals from the time of Shlomo HaMelech,
563	from the First Temple period. What became clear? That the Greeks did not
564	invent it. Who invented this structure?
565	Shlomo HaMelech.
566	And what is this idea of cylinders and a uniform line? A Torah
567	scroll. Shlomo HaMelech. They always thought it was a Greek
568	idea. It became clear that the Greeks copied it from us,
569	from Shlomo HaMelech. And when a person entered the hall of pillars,
570	he would see the pillars with the capitals above.
571	You feel that you are walking among Torah scrolls of splendid
572	marble. That is what Shlomo made. But the big question:
573	how did
574	water reach the top of the Temple Mount?
575	The Temple Mount is a high mountain and has no springs. There are
576	mountains that have springs. On the Temple Mount there is no spring
577	of water.
578	And the Beit HaMikdash needs a huge amount of
579	water. The service of the offerings was there, they slaughter
580	offerings. The floor must be washed, much
581	cleaning is needed. The House of HaShem must always be like a clean
582	palace
583	and pure. Where would you bring such quantities of water
584	to the top of the mountain? Building the Beit HaMikdash in another place
585	was not an option. The Temple Mount is where it had to
586	be built. Something
587	amazing was discovered. Shlomo
588	HaMelech took springs located at a distance of 68
589	kilometers from Yerushalayim, in Chevron.
590	And according to the law of communicating vessels, which was discovered
591	much later, but Shlomo HaMelech already knew
592	it, which says that water you put
593	into different places, they must, even if you put
594	a wide bottle and a narrow one, but they have one pipe
595	below, they always adjust themselves to be
596	at the same height. The law of communicating vessels.
597	According to the law of communicating vessels, Shlomo HaMelech dug up
598	the springs located in Chevron and arranged a system of
